question: The base of a right pyramid is a square of side 8sqrt{2} cm and each of its slant edge is of length 10 cm. What is the volume (in cm³) of the pyramid?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base Area = (8√2)² = 128 cm²

Distance from center to base vertex = Half of diagonal = (8√2 × √2) ÷ 2 = 8 cm

Height = √(Slant Edge² − Half-diagonal²) = √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6 cm

Volume = 1/3 × Base Area × Height = 1/3 × 128 × 6 = 256 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 256 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square base (a) = 8√2 cm

Slant edge (l) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of pyramid = 1/3 × Base Area × Height

Diagonal of square = a√2

Slant edge² = Height² + (Diagonal / 2)²
